prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry of an elevated industrial platform beside a raised concrete water tank, showing the tank rim and pipe within arm's reach (~0.3–1.0 m) on the right in frames 1–2, in front in frame 3, and on the left in frames 4–5 as the camera wearer turns ~180 degrees clockwise from facing the left catwalk (~1–3 m below and ahead) to facing the right staircase descending to the warehouse floor (~3–6 m below). In frames 1–2, a green valve wheel stands ~1.0–1.5 m ahead to the right inside the tank rim, while in frames 4–5 the staircase (~1–3 m ahead/below with a yellow handrail on the right) leads toward a metal cart (~4–5 m away), bags on the lower right (~3–5 m away), and a person in red standing ~5–6 m away (~1–2 m right of the cart) facing toward the staircase. The depth map clarifies the vertical drop and continuous distance gradient from the near tank wall (~0.3–0.5 m) down the stairs to the floor (~4–6 m) better than the cluttered, motion-blurred RGB strip. However, it is unreliable where it completely misses the wearer's raised right hand/arm (~0.3–0.5 m away, partly out of view at the bottom right of frame 1) that occludes the tank, smooths over the thin gaps in the yellow railings, and renders the liquid inside the tank as a flat opaque surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map correctly isolates only one true entity across the five frames: the distant person in a red shirt standing on the warehouse floor in frame 5 (~5–6 m away and below the camera wearer in the upper-right background, with their head partly cropped at the top frame edge), facing roughly toward the bottom of the stairs. In the RGB context, this person is already partly visible in frame 4 (~6–7 m away, upper right) and approaches slightly while a second person near the bottom of the stairs (~3–4 m below, ~2 m left of the person in red) is partially occluded by the yellow stair railing and blue equipment. The segmentation map provides almost no useful spatial layout beyond localizing the distant standing person in frame 5, and is highly unreliable across the sequence. Specifically, it completely misses the wearer's close right arm in frame 1 (~0.3–0.5 m away) and the person in frame 4, while falsely segmenting the overhead industrial machinery in frame 1 (~2–3 m away) as a "car", the concrete tank and floor in frame 2 (~0.4–3.0 m away) as a "bench", and the near concrete tank wall in frame 4 (~0.3–1.5 m on the left, within arm's reach) as a "person".
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely blank (black) across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons despite multiple people and limbs visible in the RGB strip. In the RGB context, the camera wearer's own right forearm and open hand are raised within ~0.3–0.5 m in the lower-right foreground of frame 1 (reaching near the tank pipe and partly extending out of the bottom frame edge) before dropping out of view as the wearer turns clockwise across frames 2–5. Meanwhile, in frames 4–5, a person in a red shirt stands on the warehouse floor ~5–6 m ahead and below (facing roughly toward the stairs/camera wearer, with their head cropped at the top edge and nothing within arm's reach except the open floor), and another person is crouched or standing near the base of the stairs ~3–4 m below (~2 m left of the person in red, within arm's reach of the blue equipment and stair base, facing left/downward and not looking at the camera wearer). Because the pose map detects nothing, it adds no spatial information beyond the RGB image and is unreliable due to severe motion blur on the wearer's close hand in frame 1 and the small scale, high downward viewing angle, and partial occlusion by railings and frame boundaries for the workers below in frames 4–5.
